title: Vehicle Removal Credit on a Cardinal Personal Auto Policy
content:
The vehicle removal credit of a Cardinal Personal Auto Policy is the amount carried by the return premium entry of a vehicle removal, for the term the removal falls in.

## Clause

The vehicle removal credit is the credit base times the short-hold share, rounded to the cent (half up) once, at the end, with no intermediate rounding.

## Definitions

- **Full-term drop.** The full-term premium before the removal less the full-term premium after it, both as recorded on the removal entry.
- **Days of the removal's term.** Counted in calendar days from the term effective date to the term expiration date of the term the removal falls in.
- **Credit days.** The calendar days from the credit start date to the term expiration date, less the loss payee notice days, and never fewer than nil.
- **Credit base.** The full-term drop times the credit days divided by the days of the removal's term.
- **Credit start date, deletion back-dating allowance, loss payee notice days and short-hold share.** The credit start date is the date the removal was recorded. The deletion back-dating allowance is nil, no loss payee notice days are deducted, and the short-hold share is one.

## Inputs and their records

| Quantity | Where it is read |
|---|---|
| Full-term premium before and after the removal | The vehicle removal entry in the policy's transaction history |
| Date the removal was recorded | The vehicle removal entry |
| Term effective and expiration dates | The policy record, for the term the removal falls in |

## Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

A removal entry shows a full-term premium of 1400.00 before the removal and 1100.00 after it. It was recorded on 1 April 2026, in a term from 1 January 2026 to 1 July 2026.

1. Full-term drop: 1400.00 less 1100.00, which is 300.00.
2. Days of the removal's term: 181.
3. Credit days: 1 April to 1 July 2026 is 91 calendar days, with nothing deducted, so 91.
4. Credit base: 300.00 times 91 divided by 181, which is 150.8287… (not rounded).
5. Credit: 150.8287… times one, rounded once to 150.83.

**Floor on the credit days.** Credit days never fall below nil, so the credit base is never negative.
